recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-13088 unless a future work group decision reopens the modifier-extension conformance rule.
issue_request: FHIR-13088 was a Published FHIR-core change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether the extensibility documentation sentence saying an unsafe-to-ignore extension must be represented differently using a Modifier Extension should use SHALL instead of must; the recorded resolution was to change it to SHALL.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied before this reconciliation by git commit bbd80926e4100a490d68f04c58ab46be57994368, 'GF#13088 - fix conformance language', which changed source/extensibility.html from 'it must be represented differently' to 'it SHALL be represented differently' on 2018-03-12. This matches the Jira comment noting SVN revision 13375.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps extension=extensibility in the active type-pages section, confirming source/extensibility.html is in current build scope. Later published edits on the same bullet, FHIR-18344 in e8cc2b24b5100dcf299406ca0db4d005a7d808ba and FHIR-19359 in 67ee800fd2ddfec4ee1fbcc42d293789a7429077, clarified the grammar and the meaning of 'Not safe' while retaining the SHALL requirement. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-13088 community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source says that if it is not safe for an application processing the content of the resource to ignore the extension, it SHALL be represented using a Modifier Extension rather than an extension element.
